transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14 | Time: 16:00 PT | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jamal Rivera (CTO, Sierra), Leah Park (Head of ML, Sierra), Tom Brooks (Product PM, Sierra)
Notes / links: Deck: https://redwood.ai/salesdeck/sierra-demo | Benchmark sheet: https://redwood.ai/bench/sierra-sample | Security packet: shared post-call

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this to about 45ish, we have a quick demo of our Eval / Quality Monitoring flow — prompt sets, regression alerts, ab comparisons, and how that surfaces in Console and Optimize
[00:18] Jamal: yeah thanks alex, quick context — we're evaluating quality monitoring to support our commerce chat assistant; key concerns are silent regressions, and being able to test A/B model changes before rolling to prod
[00:34] Priya: perfect. i'll start with the prompt sets piece then jump into regression alerts, and then show an A/B compars, sorry comparison, from a real run we did earlier this week
[00:48] Leah: quick Q, does the eval run need to see PII fields or can we mask? our compliance team wants to know
[00:55] Priya: good call. you can either mask data client-side or run in Redwood Private — the control plane doesn't retain raw inputs, and we integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest. note: some transcriptions in docs say K V cache which is fine — but for security it's KMS/H S M integrations, SAML / S S O supported
[01:15] Tom: okay fine. also how much effort to onboard prompt sets? we have 3 product flows — checkout, returns, recommendations
[01:24] Alex: onboarding's usually a few hours to a couple days depending on tagging and eval rules. we have a prompt-set schema in the Console, we can ingest csv or via API. priya — walk them through prompt sets
[01:34] Priya: sure. (screen share) so in the Console you create a prompt set, add meta tags (flow:checkout, channel:web, language:en), and attach expected outputs or evaluation metrics. you can upload a csv or point our eval pipeline at an s3 path. we store variants for A/B — e.g., prompt_v1, prompt_v2. the console auto-suggests grouping based on similarity; sometimes the nlp similarity suggestion is slightly off, it's not perfect but it's a good starting point
[01:58] Jamal: can we version-control prompt sets? we use git for prompts right now
[02:05] Priya: yep, each prompt-set has a version id, we snapshot and you can tie it to a git commit hash in metadata. you can also pin prompt+model pairs for a rollout
[02:15] Leah: show regression alerts — how do you detect regression vs expected noise? we have frequent paraphrase variants
[02:23] Priya: great Q. there are multiple signal types: automated metrics (BLEU / ROUGE is optional, but we rely more on business metrics like FCR, answer_accuracy, and embedding-similarity score against golden answers). thresholds can be set per-metric and per-prompt-tag. you can also create alert policies that combine metrics with anomaly detection — the system learns historical variance and triggers only on statistically significant drifts. here's an example — we set a baseline on embedding similarity mean 0.87 +- 0.03, and a regression alert fires if mean drops below 0.82 for two consecutive runs
[03:02] Tom: is there a way to triage false positives quickly? our ops team hates chasing noise
[03:09] Priya: yes — mute rules, alert grouping, and a triage view with sample failing chats and auto-suggested remediation playbooks. you can also attach a Jira ticket template to the alert
[03:22] Alex: and we can route alerts by severity to different channels — slack, jira, pagerduty for critical user-facing regressions
[03:31] Leah: nice. and A/B comparisons — can we run different model variants, say quantized vs full precision, and compare latency/quality tradeoffs?
[03:40] Priya: absolutely. our A/B pipeline runs both variants against the same prompt set and produces side-by-side dashboards: token-level latency, cost per 1k tokens, and quality metrics with confidence intervals. we surface paired-test statistics and uplift numbers. (shows sample) here you can see model-a (8-bit quant) is 22% cheaper but shows a 3.5% drop in answer_accuracy on returns flow
[04:04] Jamal: do you support continuous A/B where one percent of traffic gets the new model and statistics update in near-real time?
[04:12] Priya: yes — we integrate with the serving runtime to support canary rollouts and auto-rollback if certain SLOs breach. the Console shows live buckets and you can set rollout policies — e.g., increase exposure from 1% to 10% if quality delta < 1% and latency within SLO
[04:29] Tom: what about offline evaluations? we want to run nightly evals on historical queries
[04:35] Priya: that's a common pattern. you can schedule nightly eval jobs via API or Console, store results in your S3, and have regression alerts trigger on the nightly runs. we also keep historical eval dashboards and let you compare across any two dates
[04:48] Leah: curious about the Optimize recommendations — you mentioned Redwood Optimize earlier as a cost/perf toolkit
[04:54] Alex: i'll hand the demo back to priya to show Optimize suggestions for batching, quantization, and cache configs
[05:00] Priya: right. Optimize analyzes your traffic distribution (seq len, tokens per request, concurrency) and recommends batching configs and KV cache policies. it will flag prompts that benefit most from prefix-caching. there's also a 'simulate' feature — simulate quantized model latency/cost given your token distribution. note: simulation is an estimate not perfect, we encourage a short benchmark run
[05:23] Jamal: how invasive is the benchmark? we want to keep infra impact low
[05:28] Priya: benchmark runs are our standard: we replay 10k customer-supplied prompts against selected model variants in an isolated job. it can run on hosted infra or on your private cluster if you're using Redwood Private. time-wise it's usually a few hours depending on throughput you request
[05:42] Leah: earlier you said console suggests grouping and sometimes it's off — can we provide our own labelling rules to avoid noisy clusters?
[05:49] Priya: yes, you can provide deterministic label rules (regex, metadata fields) and disable auto-grouping. also we store raw and normalized tokens so you can tune pre-processing
[05:58] Tom: show us an example alert flow and a failing sample please
[06:04] Priya: (navigates) here's an alert from last week — regression on returns flow. clicking opens the triage: we show 10 example interactions, highlight changed tokens, show delta in embedding similarity and a small suggested runbook: "try prompt fallback to v1, or increase temperature clamp" — note: some of these auto-suggestions read a bit generic in transcripts but are helpful as a first pass
[06:35] Alex: to hit some of your procurement/security items — we support SC IM, SAML SSO, audit logs, and customer-managed keys. priya will share the SOC2 + security packet after the call
[06:48] Jamal: excellent — cost model? pricing for hosted evals vs dedicated pilot?
[06:54] Alex: hosted eval runs priced per-run + per-token; for a dedicated pilot or Dedicated capacity we can do a committed monthly with discounts. i'll send a pilot pricing sheet. for quick reference: small benchmark (~10k prompts, 3 model variants) is typically in the low thousands USD range, varies on throughput and retention needs
[07:13] Leah: let's talk about data retention — how long do you keep eval data? we need 90 day retention for compliance reasons
[07:18] Priya: you can set retention policies per project, default is 30 days but we support custom retention up to customer needs — with Private you can enforce zero retention and full audit logging
[07:29] Jamal: any nuance with private deployments and eval pipelines?
[07:33] Priya: we ship an agent to run evals inside your VPC/air-gapped environment; results can be sent to your internal S3. the control plane can be configured to only store metadata and not raw transcripts if you want
[07:47] Tom: ok on technical feasibility. what's the pilot scope you'd propose?
[07:51] Alex: propose a 2-week pilot: week 1 onboarding + run a 2-day benchmark (10k prompts across 3 flows), week 2 analyze results and run an A/B canary on a small traffic slice. deliverables: benchmark report, dashboard access, alert policies configured, and a short runbook for triage
[08:10] Leah: that sounds reasonable. timeline — we want pilot started in late May if possible
[08:16] Alex: we can start week of May 25th; we'll need Leah's prompt sets and Jamal's infra contact to provision if you're using Private
[08:25] Jamal: i'll confirm internal folks by Monday
[08:29] Tom: quick question on metrics — can you plug in product metrics like revenue per session as an eval metric?
[08:35] Priya: yes. we accept custom metrics — you can upload a metric mapping file linking eval interactions to downstream events (revenue, conversion). we can compute uplift across variants and show impact with confidence intervals
[08:49] Leah: how do you handle paraphrase-heavy prompts for evaluation — embedding similarity sometimes fails for short utterances
[08:56] Priya: for short utterances we recommend multiple signals — embedding similarity + token overlap + human-labeled subset for calibration. we also support human-in-the-loop labeling to bootstrap thresholds
[09:09] Jamal: any references / case studies?
[09:12] Alex: we ran a similar pilot with Ember Finance — decreased false regressions by 40% and caught a model drift before a rollout. i'll share that case study link after the call
[09:22] Leah: i assume logs / traces are available per-eval?
[09:25] Priya: yes — per-eval artifacts include raw candidate outputs, token-level latencies, and the KV cache hit rates if applicable (sometimes transcribed as K V cache in notes).
[09:38] Tom: are there any gotchas for async vs streaming responses in evals? we use streaming for long form answers on recommendations
[09:45] Priya: streaming is supported, but you need to capture latencies at stream-chunk granularity. Optimize simulates streaming too but benchmarks are recommended for accurate tail latency numbers
[09:57] Alex: ok want to open it up for final Qs and then recap next steps
[10:02] Jamal: one more — does Redwood support model fallbacks automatically when a regression is detected in prod?
[10:09] Priya: yes — there are automated rollback and fallback policies. you can configure a fallback model (e.g., older stable checkpoint) and set automatic triggers based on quality or latency SLOs
[10:19] Leah: great. final — can you show the API for kicking off an eval?
[10:23] Priya: quick snippet: POST /v1/evals with body {prompt_set_id, model_variants, eval_config} — you can pass expected_output or golden_answers. response includes eval_id and webhook for completion. note: some SDK docs have a small typo where param 'golden_answers' was documented as 'gold_answer' — we'll fix that in the docs
[10:43] Tom: ha, classic.
[10:45] Alex: recap: we'll run a 2-day benchmark (Alex to send pricing + SOW), Priya to share security packet and eval templates, Leah to provide prompt sets, Jamal to confirm infra contacts. scheduled follow-up: benchmark kickoff call week of May 25th.
[10:59] Jamal: thanks everyone, this was really helpful
[11:01] Alex: thanks all — we'll follow up in notes and slack

End of transcript
